about: What each kind of object needs before it can be installed (Q6619: the RFI is what the build produces when it cannot complete an object the way the codes and trade practice require). One requirement per entry: the objects it applies to, the property that meets it, the code section or trade rule behind it, the question it asks when no document meets it, the build step it must be answered before, and how the build completes the object meanwhile (a proposal marked unsure). Rules data, never job values.

steps.label: rough-in in walls and above ceilings

topic_steps.starts: lighting: fixture leg with no switch

requirements.basis: NEC 210.11: branch circuits are provided for every load; a luminaire is an outlet (NEC Article 100) supplied by a branch circuit, its homerun to a panel

requirements.what: a fixture type the light fixture schedule lists
requirements.basis: the light fixture schedule gives each type's product, voltage, wattage and mounting; its box and support (NEC 314.27(A), 410.36) and its share of the circuit's load (NEC 220.14) follow from the type

requirements.what: a control (a switch, sensor or contactor, or unswitched by design)
requirements.basis: IECC C405.2: interior lighting has manual and automatic controls (C405.2.1 to C405.2.3); a switch is wired to the load it controls (NEC 404.2); emergency and exit lighting is unswitched by design (NEC 700.21)
NEC 210.11: every receptacle outlet is supplied by a branch circuit (NEC 210.52 for where they are required, 210.21(B) for their rating against the circuit)
NEC 210.11: every load is on a branch circuit; an equipment connection's circuit, conductors and protection come from the equipment's nameplate (NEC 440.32 to 440.35, 430.22, 422.10)
requirements.ask: Which circuit feeds it, at what rating?

requirements.basis: a switch or sensor is wired to the load it controls (NEC 404.2); a control the plans tie to no luminaire or load cannot be wired, and the lights it was meant for are left without control (IECC C405.2)

requirements.what: a branch circuit at its nameplate rating
requirements.basis: NEC 210.11 and 440.4/430.6: every piece of utilization equipment is supplied by a branch circuit sized from its nameplate (MCA and MOCP, NEC 440.32 to 440.35, 430.22, 422.10), with its disconnect within sight (NEC 440.14, 430.102)
requirements.ask: Which circuit feeds it, and where is its disconnect?

requirements.what: a feeder from the gear upstream
requirements.basis: NEC 215.2 and 408.36: every panelboard is fed by a feeder sized for its load with its overcurrent protection; the one-line or riser names the gear that feeds it
requirements.ask: Which gear feeds it, with what feeder?

requirements.what: a breaker in its panel's schedule
requirements.basis: NEC 408.4(A): every circuit is identified at its panel by its breaker, and NEC 210.11 gives every load a branch circuit; a circuit the plans use that no panel schedule has (or a panel no document has) has no breaker to land on
requirements.ask: Which panel and breaker feed it: is the schedule short a row, or the plans' circuit label wrong?

requirements.basis: NEC 408.4(A): each circuit's load is identified; a breaker the schedule loads with nothing on the plans is a load nobody has located, or a row to make a spare
requirements.ask: Where is its load, or is it a spare?

requirements.what: a panel on the plans to hold its breakers
requirements.basis: NEC 408.36 and 110.26: each scheduled panelboard is installed with its working space; a schedule with no panel on any plan has no place to be set
